newsitem.title: UK: British twins born 19 days apart.
newsitem.headline: British twins born 19 days apart.

text.p: A British woman has given birth to twin girls 19 days apart.
The girls, being nurtured in an incubator, were even born in different years and their mother celebrated her own birthday in between, the Daily Mirror newspaper reported on Friday.
Paige Speakman was born 14 weeks prematurely on December 19. Her sister Abbey did not follow for another 19 days.
"Abbey just decided she wasn't going to follow her sister. She kicked Paige out to make more room for herself," their mother, Tracy Speakman, told the tabloid, adding:
"It was a very weird sensation still being pregnant after already giving birth. I had my own birthday in between the births so I was 23 when I had Paige and 24 when I had Abbey."
Doctors say the non-identical twins came from two separate eggs. They each had their own placenta supplying nutrients and their own amniotic sac.
